source.statement: The gamma_p framework specializes at p=1 to Huber regression and yields a high-probability (1+epsilon)-approximate solution in O~(r sqrt(mn)/epsilon + poly(n,1/epsilon)) quantum time.

counterexample_family: Fix a proper gamma_1/Huber family with m=16,n=2,r=1 and epsilon tending to zero. Corollary 12 quantifies over every epsilon>0 and explicitly applies QGLMSparsify, but its M=Theta~(n/epsilon^2) call violates the cited MultiSample precondition M<=m.
negative_control: At epsilon=sqrt(n/m), the MultiSample domain condition is satisfied.
result: The Huber identity is valid; the proposed all-epsilon gamma-framework algorithm is not defined by its cited primitive on an assumption-satisfying family. This does not rule out a repaired algorithm with epsilon=Omega(sqrt(n/m)).
